cards.explanation: The answer is flee. Paul says, “But you, O man of God, flee from these things…” (1 Timothy 6:11). Just before this, he warned about the love of money (1 Timothy 6:10), so these are the things Timothy is told to run from. FLEE, friends. Nobody flees at a stroll.

The answer is pursue them. Paul says to “…pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.” Notice the two directions. Flee from the money trap, and pursue this list. Same legs, different direction, friends, and I'd say the second direction is the better workout.

The answer is eternal. Paul says, “Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called…” (1 Timothy 6:12). Timothy was called to it, so he's told to grab hold of it, like you'd grab a rope you were just thrown. Eternal is a lot longer than any batch I've ever baked.

The answer is False. Paul says Timothy made the good confession “…before many witnesses.” (1 Timothy 6:12). Many, friends, so it wasn't private with no one else around. The text doesn't say where it happened, but it does say people were there. I bet that's a moment you'd remember.

The answer is Pontius Pilate. Paul says Christ Jesus “…made the good confession in His testimony before Pontius Pilate…” Pilate was the governor Jesus was handed over to (Matthew 27:2). So Paul points Timothy to Jesus' own example. Timothy confessed before many witnesses, and Jesus made His confession before Pilate.

The answer is until Jesus Christ appears. Paul says to keep the commandment “…without stain or reproach until the appearance of our Lord Jesus Christ…” So Timothy keeps going until Jesus appears. No finish line he can set for himself, friends. It's a keep-the-oven-on kind of job.

The answer is False. Paul gives no date. He says the Sovereign One will bring it about “…in His own time.” (1 Timothy 6:15). Jesus says nobody knows the day or hour except the Father (Matthew 24:36). So no circling dates on the calendar, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says it plainly: “No one has ever seen Him, nor can anyone see Him.” He says it right after saying that the Sovereign One dwells in unapproachable light (1 Timothy 6:16). Unapproachable light, friends, and I'll let Paul's words stand.

The answer is with praise and an Amen. Paul finishes with, “To Him be honor and eternal dominion! Amen.” After saying who the Sovereign One is, he ends with praise. I think that's a fitting way to close after a description like that.

The answer is God. Paul says to put hope “…in God, who richly provides all things for us to enjoy.” Wealth can't hold that kind of hope. God can. I like the sound of that, because my own hopes got a lot safer once they left the junk drawer I used to be stuck in.

The answer is True. Paul calls it “…the uncertainty of wealth…” That's why the hope goes in God instead. Money can be here today and gone before the cookies cool. Paul says it's uncertain, friends, and I'd say that's honest.

The answer is good works. Paul tells Timothy to instruct the rich “…to do good, to be rich in good works…” See what he did there, friends? Same word, new meaning. Rich in good works. That's a bank account I can get behind.
The answer is share. Paul says to be “…generous and ready to share…” Ready is the word I like, friends. Not “eventually.” Like the guy who's already got the cookie box open when you walk in.

The answer is a firm foundation for the future. Paul says they are “…treasuring up for themselves a firm foundation for the future…” Giving feels like losing something, but Paul says it builds something. It's a foundation, friends, the part of the bakery nobody sees but everything stands on. I'd call that a smart investment.

The answer is empty chatter and opposing arguments. Paul says to avoid “…irreverent, empty chatter…” and the opposing arguments of so-called “knowledge.” That's a lot of talk with nothing inside it. It's like a cookie box that's all ribbon and no cookies.

The answer is False. Paul says some have professed this so-called “knowledge” and “…thus swerved away from the faith.” Swerved, friends, like a car drifting out of its lane. That's why he told Timothy to avoid it.

The answer is grace. Paul closes with, “Grace be with you all.” After all that fighting, guarding and fleeing, the blessing he leaves them with is grace. I like how that lands, friends. It's like the last batch coming out warm.
